title: Where are you from?
goal: Say where you're from, what you do, and which languages you speak — while mastering 是, 不, and 嗎, the three words behind almost all your first sentences.
bekal: build "A is B" sentences with 是 and negate them with 不是
turn any sentence into a question with 嗎 without changing the word order
avoid the biggest trap for English speakers: putting 是 before an adjective

dialogs.title: 對話 — 在學生餐廳
dialogs.intro: Day two. Budi and Xiaomei are lining up in the campus cafeteria. A friend of Xiaomei's joins them.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [布迪|Bùdí]，[這是|zhè shì][我朋友|wǒ péngyǒu][阿明|Ā Míng]。
lines.id: Budi, this is my friend A-Ming.
lines.literal: Budi, this — is — I — friend — A-Ming.

lines.speaker: 阿明:
lines.text: [你好|Nǐ hǎo]！[你是|Nǐ shì][哪國人|nǎ guó rén]？
lines.literal: you — good! you — are — which — country — person?

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [我是|Wǒ shì][印尼人|Yìnní rén]。[你呢|Nǐ ne]？

lines.speaker: 阿明:
lines.text: [我是|Wǒ shì][台灣人|Táiwān rén]，[台南來的|Táinán lái de]。
lines.literal: I — am — Taiwan — person, Tainan — come — (one).

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [我是|Wǒ shì]，[可是|kěshì][阿明|Ā Míng][不是|bú shì]。
lines.literal: I — am, but — A-Ming — not — is.

lines.speaker: 阿明:
lines.text: [我是|Wǒ shì][老師|lǎoshī]。[我教|Wǒ jiāo][英文|Yīngwén]。
lines.id: I'm a teacher. I teach English.
lines.literal: I — am — teacher. I — teach — English — language.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [真的|Zhēn de][嗎|ma]？[你|Nǐ][看起來|kànqǐlái][很年輕|hěn niánqīng]。

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [我學|Wǒ xué][電腦|diànnǎo]。[中文|Zhōngwén][是|shì][我的|wǒ de][第二|dì-èr][專長|zhuāncháng]。
lines.id: I study computer science. Chinese is my second major.
lines.literal: I — study — computer. Chinese — is — I — 's — second — specialty.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [你|Nǐ][會說|huì shuō][印尼話|Yìnní huà][和|hàn][英文|Yīngwén][嗎|ma]？
lines.id: Can you speak Indonesian and English?
lines.literal: you — can — speak — Indonesia — speech — and — English — (question)?

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [會|Huì]。[還有|Hái yǒu][一點|yìdiǎn][爪哇話|Zhǎowā huà]。
lines.literal: can. still — have — a-little — Java — speech.

lines.speaker: 阿明:
lines.text: [哇|Wā]，[三種|sān zhǒng][語言|yǔyán]！[你|Nǐ][不簡單|bù jiǎndān][喔|o]！
lines.literal: wow, three — kind — language! you — not — simple — (wow)!

notes: ⚠️ **和 ("and") is pronounced *hàn* by most Taiwanese**, not *hé* as mainland textbooks teach. Both are understood; *hàn* sounds local. It is one of the most distinctive Taiwanese pronunciations.
**呢 bounces a question back without repeating it.** *我是印尼人。你呢？* — "I'm Indonesian. And you?" Attach 呢 to any noun and it means "what about …?". Very economical, and used constantly.
**都 (*dōu*, "all") stands before the verb, not before the people.** *你們都是學生嗎？* — not *都你們*. The rule: 都 always comes **after** what it sums up and **before** the verb.

**啦 (*la*) and 喔 (*o*) are the two Taiwanese particles you'll hear most.** 啦 softens a sentence, a bit like "you know" or "come on"; 喔 adds a gentle warning or an affectionate tone. Without them your sentences are correct but sound like a public announcement.
⚠️ **印尼話 and 印尼文 both mean "Indonesian"**, but 話 stresses the **spoken** language and 文 the **written** one. To say "I can speak Indonesian", 印尼話 fits better.

grammars.title: 是: the verb that links two nouns — and nothing else
body: **是** means "to be", and it has just one job: linking **two nouns**. A 是 B means "A is B". It is negated with 不是, never with 沒是.
after: ⚠️ **Here is the biggest trap in this unit: 是 is NOT used before adjectives.** English says "I *am* Indonesian" and "I *am* busy" — the same "am" both times. Mandarin keeps the two strictly apart.
**我是忙。** ✗ wrong. **我很忙。** ✓ right. Adjectives don't need 是; what goes in front of them is 很. Unit 14 covers this in full, but plant it now: **nouns take 是, adjectives take 很.**
⚠️ Notice too that 不 before 是 is pronounced **bú**, not *bù* — because 是 is fourth tone. This book always prints the tone that is actually spoken.

grammars.title: 嗎: questions without flipping anything
body: Here is Mandarin's gift to you. To make a yes/no question, **attach 嗎 to the end of a statement**. Nothing is flipped, nothing moves, nothing else is added.
after: ⚠️ **Your voice must not rise at the end.** This is the hardest habit for English speakers to break: we mark questions with rising intonation, and the habit carries over. In Mandarin, 嗎 already marks the question; raising your pitch only turns your last word into a different word.
**How to answer: repeat the verb.** Mandarin has no single word for "yes". *你是學生嗎？* is answered **是** (yes) or **不是** (no). *你會說中文嗎？* is answered **會** or **不會**.
**The A-不-A form is a second option**, a bit more casual and very common in Taiwan: *你**是不是**學生？* *你**會不會**說中文？* The meaning is exactly the same; 嗎 is never used together with this form.

blocks.text: The pattern is very regular: **country + 人** = its people, **country + 文** = its language. Once you know the country's name, the other two words come free.

⚠️ Note that **中文** is used in both Taiwan and China for "Chinese". In Taiwan you'll also hear **國語** (*Guóyǔ*, "national language") and **華語** (*Huáyǔ*). What is **not** used in Taiwan is 普通話 (*pǔtōnghuà*) — that is the mainland term. And **台語** (*Táiyǔ*) is a different language altogether: Taiwanese Hokkien, spoken at home by more than half the population.

blocks.title: Asking about jobs
items: **你做什麼工作？** *Nǐ zuò shénme gōngzuò?* — What do you do?
**我是工程師。** *Wǒ shì gōngchéngshī.* — I'm an engineer.
**我在銀行工作。** *Wǒ zài yínháng gōngzuò.* — I work at a bank.
**我還是學生。** *Wǒ háishì xuéshēng.* — I'm still a student.
⚠️ **老闆 is also how you address any shopkeeper** — at a night market, a food stall, a repair shop. It is polite and warm, not flattering.

sections.title: 都, 也, and 還: three little words with a fixed place

blocks.text: All three are **adverbs**, and Mandarin adverbs have one place: **after the subject, before the verb**. That place never changes, and putting them anywhere else is a mistake people hear instantly.

head: Word
Meaning
Example
Translation
rows: the order is always 也都

blocks.text: ⚠️ When all three appear together, the order is **也 → 都 → 還**: *我們**也都還**是學生。* "We're all still students too." This order is fixed and non-negotiable — luckily, sentences with all three at once are rare.

exercises.prompt: Fill in with 是, 不是, 很, or 都.
Turn these into questions with 嗎.
Put the words in the right order.
items: 嗎 / 你 / 學生 / 是
也 / 我 / 是 / 印尼人
都 / 我們 / 學生 / 是
不是 / 他 / 台灣人
